what: Multiple photo cells (7 in the original) flow endlessly, packed along a staircase rising from the lower left to the upper right of the panel. Each cell’s width is set by dividing by the bell curve value of its position on the staircase (0~1, center 1, both ends 0), so the center cell is largest and end cells shrink to 0, vanish, then regrow at the opposite end. Each cell is shifted down by 1/3 of cell height × position so the stairs look overlapped, and the image inside scales up by 1 + (1 − scale) × .7 the smaller the cell gets. It drifts on its own at .001 per frame, scrolling across the panel (panel top at screen top → panel bottom at screen top) pushes it a further (1 − 1/count) of one lap, and reversing the scroll reverses the auto drift too. On attach, the cells switch on with .5s power2.out.

options.base: Default cell width (share of panel width) — baseline for scale 1, default 5/12 (.4167)
options.drift: Auto-flow amount (share of one turn per frame), default .001 — at 0 it flows by scroll only
options.depth: Zoom share of the artwork in the small cell, default .7
options.lift: Each layer drops by the cell height divided by this number × its index and overlaps, default 3
options.fade: Duration of the on state when stuck (sec), default .5
options.trigger: Ancestor selector that sets the scroll start (from when its top edge touches the top of the screen) — if none, the panel itself
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Flow cell (direct child of the panel) — first child in the cell is a photo (placeholder)

use: … Seven cells
note: The panel is given only a size, and cells go out of the panel (upward), so overflow is not hidden. The original overlays a big title on the panel (panel at z −1) and stairs flow beneath the title. The first ‘w → 0, 1s expo.out’ of the original scroll-share tween did nothing at the starting position, so it was dropped
